record.what_it_does: Datadog is a unified observability and security platform (metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, monitors, incidents, security signals) that exposes nearly all of its functionality via a REST API.
record.auth_notes: The core API uses a DD-API-KEY header plus a DD-APPLICATION-KEY header (application keys inherit the creating user's/service account's permissions and can be scoped). OAuth2 is documented for building third-party integrations, but OAuth clients can only be tested inside the developer's own 'partner developer organization' and must be published/reviewed by Datadog before they can authorize other customers' accounts — so OAuth2 is not usable standalone by a generic multi-tenant agent toolkit without going through Datadog's integration partner/publishing process.
record.access_notes: Any signed-up user can generate API keys and application keys immediately from Organization Settings with no approval step (docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/api-app-keys). Datadog also offers a perpetually free Infrastructure Monitoring tier (up to 5 hosts) in addition to a 14-day free trial of the full platform ('Try Datadog for 14 days...'); could not fetch the exact free-tier pricing tab text (JS-rendered tabs) to quote verbatim, so treat the free-infra-tier claim as corroborated by third-party sources rather than a directly fetched primary quote.

evidence.quote: Authenticate to the API with an API key using the header `DD-API-KEY`. For some endpoints, you also need an Application key
Datadog uses the OAuth 2.0 (OAuth2) Authorization Framework to allow users to securely authorize third-party applications' access
Application keys, in conjunction with your organization's API key, give users access to Datadog's programmatic API
The Datadog API is an HTTP REST API.
Webhooks enable you to: Connect to your services. Alert your services when a metric alert is triggered.
The Datadog MCP Server acts as a bridge between your observability data in Datadog and any AI agents that support the Model Context Protocol

record.open_questions: Could not fetch a verbatim primary-source quote for the perpetual free Infrastructure Monitoring tier (pricing page uses JS tabs the fetch tool couldn't target), though it is well-corroborated by secondary sources and by the unrestricted key-creation flow. Also unclear exactly how narrow OAuth2 access is for non-partner developers versus using API/App keys for equivalent functionality.
